q: What are the warning signs in a carbon footprint report from a consultant?
title: Warning signs in a carbon footprint report
short: The main warning signs are totals with no activity data behind them, factors with no source or version, a missing boundary, carbon credits subtracted from emissions, spend-based Scope 3 presented as precise, and suspiciously round numbers. Any one of these means you cannot check the figure yourself.
audience: MSMEs and buyers reviewing a paid carbon report

sections.h: Signs the figures cannot be traced
ul: Scope totals with no litres, kWh, tonnes or kilometres beside them.
Factors given as numbers only, with no publisher, edition or year.
No list of the documents used, such as which months of electricity bills.
Totals rounded to the nearest 100 or 1,000 tonnes with no stated uncertainty.
No statement of which entity and sites are covered, or which consolidation approach was used.
No reporting period, or a period that does not match your financial year.
No mention of exclusions at all. Every real inventory leaves something out, and the GHG Protocol asks for exclusions to be disclosed.

sections.h: Signs the result is presented better than it is
ul: Carbon credits or RECs subtracted inside the Scope 1 or Scope 2 total instead of shown separately.
Scope 3 built entirely from spend, with no note that spend-based figures carry wide uncertainty.
A claim of reduction with no base year, or a base year that changed without explanation.
Words like certified, audited or verified with no named verification body, standard or statement.

sections.h: How to raise it with the preparer
p: Ask for the working file: one row per source, with quantity, unit, factor, factor source and result. A sound report can produce this in a day. If the preparer cannot, treat the total as an estimate and say so wherever you use it.
